name: ai_element_filter
title: Find elements by criteria
description: Query elements by category (BuiltInCategory name or display name), element class name (e.g. Wall, FamilyInstance, Floor), family type id, visibility in the current view and/or a bounding box in millimetres. Returns rich per-element info (type, family, level, location, bounding box, key parameters) so the AI can answer questions such as 'walls taller than 5 m'. At least one of filterCategory, filterElementType or filterFamilySymbolId is required. [Registry tool v1, Data, transaction=none. Registry tools run stored, reviewed C# inside Revit — prefer them over execute_revit_code for the same task.]

filterElementType.description: Revit API class name: Wall, Floor, FamilyInstance, Level, Grid, ...

filterFamilySymbolId.description: ElementId of a FamilySymbol; only instances of that type

filterVisibleInCurrentView.description: Only elements visible in the active view

name: analyze_model_statistics
title: Analyze model statistics
description: Model audit: total elements, types, families, views, sheets; per-category counts (optionally broken down by family/type) and per-level element distribution (elevations in mm). [Registry tool v1, Data, transaction=none. Registry tools run stored, reviewed C# inside Revit — prefer them over execute_revit_code for the same task.]

includeDetailedTypes.description: Break each category down by family and type

topCategories.description: Maximum categories to list (largest first, 0 = all)

name: cancel_execution
title: Cancel running script
description: Signals cancellation to the script currently running in the host application. Cancellation is cooperative: the script stops at its next `ct` check, and its transaction group is rolled back. Returns whether anything was running.

name: color_elements
title: Colour elements by parameter value
description: In the active view, colour every element of a category (BuiltInCategory or display name) by the value of a parameter: each distinct value gets its own colour (random palette, a gradient, or your customColors in order). Returns the legend (value → colour → count). Undo with operate_element ResetIsolate? No — clear overrides via the view's Visibility/Graphics or run again with another parameter. [Registry tool v1, View, transaction=auto. Registry tools run stored, reviewed C# inside Revit — prefer them over execute_revit_code for the same task.]

parameterName.description: Instance or type parameter name, e.g. 'Type Name', 'Level', 'Comments', 'Mark'

dryRun.description: Run the tool, then roll everything back. Use first on a model you care about.

name: create_dimensions
title: Create dimensions
description: Create linear dimensions in a plan/section view (active view by default). Either give elementIds (walls, columns, grids, family instances — one reference per element, the planar face or datum best aligned with the start→end direction) or leave them empty to auto-detect the nearest wall/grid/column at startPoint and endPoint. linePoint moves the dimension line; coordinates in mm. [Registry tool v1, Annotation, transaction=auto. Registry tools run stored, reviewed C# inside Revit — prefer them over execute_revit_code for the same task.]

linePoint.description: Optional point the dimension line passes through; default = 1000 mm beside the segment

elementIds.description: Elements to dimension between; empty = auto-detect at the two points

dryRun.description: Run the tool, then roll everything back. Use first on a model you care about.

name: create_grid
title: Create grid system
description: Create a rectangular grid: X-axis grids are vertical lines at xStartPosition + i·xSpacing running from yExtentMin to yExtentMax; Y-axis grids are horizontal lines at yStartPosition + j·ySpacing running from xExtentMin to xExtentMax. Labels alphabetic (A, B, … Z, AA) or numeric (1, 2, …); names already used get a suffix. All lengths in mm. [Registry tool v1, Architecture, transaction=auto. Registry tools run stored, reviewed C# inside Revit — prefer them over execute_revit_code for the same task.]

xSpacing.description: Spacing between X-axis grids in mm

ySpacing.description: Spacing between Y-axis grids in mm

xStartPosition.description: X of the first vertical grid (mm)

yStartPosition.description: Y of the first horizontal grid (mm)

xExtentMin.description: Where horizontal grids start (mm); default = xStartPosition − 1000

xExtentMax.description: Where horizontal grids end (mm); default = last X grid + 1000

yExtentMin.description: Where vertical grids start (mm); default = yStartPosition − 1000

yExtentMax.description: Where vertical grids end (mm); default = last Y grid + 1000

elevation.description: Z of the grid lines in mm

dryRun.description: Run the tool, then roll everything back. Use first on a model you care about.

name: create_level
title: Create levels
description: Create one or more levels at elevations in millimetres (from project origin), optionally with a floor plan and/or ceiling plan view each. Existing level names are skipped and reported. Use dryRun first on a shared model. [Registry tool v1, Architecture, transaction=auto. Registry tools run stored, reviewed C# inside Revit — prefer them over execute_revit_code for the same task.]

dryRun.description: Run the tool, then roll everything back. Use first on a model you care about.

name: create_line_based_element
title: Create line-based elements
description: Create walls, beams (structural framing), ducts, pipes, conduits, cable trays or any line-based family instance from start/end points in mm. baseLevel is an elevation in mm — the nearest level is used and the remainder becomes the base offset. Walls: thickness picks/creates a wall type of that width, height is the unconnected height. Beams/MEP curves use the points' Z as absolute elevation. Give typeId (from get_available_family_types) to pick a specific type; otherwise the first type of the category is used and reported. [Registry tool v1, Generic, transaction=auto. Registry tools run stored, reviewed C# inside Revit — prefer them over execute_revit_code for the same task.]

category.description: OST_Walls, OST_StructuralFraming, OST_DuctCurves, OST_PipeCurves, OST_Conduit, OST_CableTray, or a category with line-based families

typeId.description: ElementId of the type to use (optional)

thickness.description: Wall width / duct width / pipe diameter in mm (optional)

height.description: Wall height in mm (default 3000) / duct height

baseLevel.description: Base elevation in mm (nearest level is used)

baseOffset.description: Offset from the base level in mm

dryRun.description: Run the tool, then roll everything back. Use first on a model you care about.

name: create_point_based_element
title: Create point-based elements
description: Place family instances at points in mm: doors and windows (hosted in a wall — hostWallId or the nearest wall within 1500 mm), furniture, columns, generic models, etc. Category is taken from typeId when given; otherwise pass category and the first loaded type is used. rotation in degrees about Z; facingFlipped flips doors/windows. width/height/depth are applied only when the instance exposes writable parameters of those names. [Registry tool v1, Architecture, transaction=auto. Registry tools run stored, reviewed C# inside Revit — prefer them over execute_revit_code for the same task.]

name.description: Free text label for the report

category.description: BuiltInCategory when typeId is omitted, e.g. OST_Doors, OST_Windows, OST_Furniture, OST_StructuralColumns, OST_GenericModel

baseLevel.description: Base elevation in mm (nearest level is used)

dryRun.description: Run the tool, then roll everything back. Use first on a model you care about.

name: create_room
title: Create rooms
description: Place rooms at points in mm inside enclosed wall boundaries and set name, number, department, comments and limits. Level from levelId or the nearest level to the point's Z. Reports whether each room ended up enclosed (area > 0). [Registry tool v1, Architecture, transaction=auto. Registry tools run stored, reviewed C# inside Revit — prefer them over execute_revit_code for the same task.]

upperLimitId.description: Level ElementId for the upper limit

dryRun.description: Run the tool, then roll everything back. Use first on a model you care about.

name: create_structural_framing_system
title: Create beam system
description: Create a Revit BeamSystem inside a rectangle (mm) on a named level: beams at fixed spacing, running perpendicular to the chosen edge, with beginning/center/end justification. beamTypeName matches a loaded structural framing family or type name (first one otherwise). A missing level named 'Level N' is created at N × 4000 mm, as in the reference implementation. [Registry tool v1, Structure, transaction=auto. Registry tools run stored, reviewed C# inside Revit — prefer them over execute_revit_code for the same task.]

directionEdge.description: Beams run perpendicular to this edge

elevation.description: Optional absolute elevation in mm; default = level elevation

dryRun.description: Run the tool, then roll everything back. Use first on a model you care about.

name: create_surface_based_element
title: Create floors, ceilings and roofs
description: Create floors (default), ceilings or footprint roofs from a closed outer loop of line segments in mm. baseLevel is an elevation in mm (nearest level + offset). thickness picks or creates a floor/ceiling type of that thickness when typeId is omitted. [Registry tool v1, Architecture, transaction=auto. Registry tools run stored, reviewed C# inside Revit — prefer them over execute_revit_code for the same task.]

thickness.description: Slab thickness in mm (floors/ceilings, when typeId omitted)

baseLevel.description: Elevation in mm (nearest level is used)

dryRun.description: Run the tool, then roll everything back. Use first on a model you care about.

name: delete_element
title: Delete elements
description: Delete elements by id. Revit also removes dependents (tags, dimensions, hosted elements); the response counts both. Use dryRun=true first to see what would go. [Registry tool v1, Generic, transaction=auto. Registry tools run stored, reviewed C# inside Revit — prefer them over execute_revit_code for the same task.]

dryRun.description: Run the tool, then roll everything back. Use first on a model you care about.

name: execute_revit_code
title: Execute C# in Revit
description: Runs a C# script inside the open Revit session with the user's full privileges. Globals: doc (Document), uidoc (UIDocument), app (Application), uiapp (UIApplication), ct (CancellationToken — check it inside long loops), log(string) to append output, progress(int current, int total, string message) to report progress, args (data passed in the `args` parameter: args.Str/Double/Int/Long/Bool(key, fallback), args.Obj(key), args.List(key), args.Has(key), args.Require(key)). Prefer args over literals for anything that may change between calls — a script whose text stays identical compiles once and is cached. End with `return <value>;` to send a result; Revit objects are summarised (ElementId as number, XYZ as {x,y,z} in feet, Element as {id,name,category}). Default usings: System, System.Linq, System.Collections.Generic, Autodesk.Revit.DB, Autodesk.Revit.UI, Autodesk.Revit.DB.Structure. All model changes land in one undoable group named 'MCP: <label>'. Use dryRun=true first for anything destructive. Fails with isError=true and diagnostics when the code does not compile, throws, is blocked by the guard, or exceeds the timeout; nothing is committed in those cases. Requires the user to have enabled code execution in the HPRebar MCP Bridge window inside Revit.

code.description: C# script body, max 32 KB. No `await`, no System.IO / System.Net / System.Diagnostics.Process / reflection (blocked by the guard).

transaction.description: auto (default): the bridge wraps the script in one Transaction. manual: the script opens its own Transaction(s) inside one TransactionGroup. none: read-only; any modification fails.

dryRun.description: Run the script, then roll everything back. Use first for destructive changes.

timeoutSeconds.description: Cooperative timeout in seconds, 5–120. The script sees it through `ct`.

label.description: Short name shown in Revit's Undo history as 'MCP: <label>'. Max 64 characters.

args.description: Optional JSON object handed to the script as `args` (e.g. {"spacing": 150, "names": ["A","B"]}). Keys are matched case-insensitively.

name: export_room_data
title: Export room data
description: All rooms with name, number, level, area (m²), volume (m³), perimeter (mm), unbounded height (mm), department, comments, occupancy and phase. Unplaced and not-enclosed rooms are excluded unless requested. [Registry tool v1, Architecture, transaction=none. Registry tools run stored, reviewed C# inside Revit — prefer them over execute_revit_code for the same task.]

name: get_available_family_types
title: Get available family types
description: Loaded family types (FamilySymbol) plus system types (wall, floor, roof, ceiling, curtain system) in the project. Filter by BuiltInCategory names and/or a partial family or type name. Returns the type ids other create_* tools need. [Registry tool v1, Generic, transaction=none. Registry tools run stored, reviewed C# inside Revit — prefer them over execute_revit_code for the same task.]

familyNameFilter.description: Case-insensitive substring matched against family name and type name

limit.description: Maximum types to return (0 = no limit)

name: get_current_view_elements
title: Get elements in the current view
description: Elements visible in the active view, filtered by model and/or annotation categories (BuiltInCategory names such as OST_Walls, OST_Doors, OST_Dimensions). Without filters a default set of common model + annotation categories is used. Locations and lengths are reported in millimetres. [Registry tool v1, View, transaction=none. Registry tools run stored, reviewed C# inside Revit — prefer them over execute_revit_code for the same task.]

includeHidden.description: Include elements hidden in the view

limit.description: Maximum elements to return (0 = no limit)

annotations.title: Get elements in the current view

name: get_current_view_info
title: Get current view info
description: Details of the active Revit view: id, name, view type, scale, detail level, discipline, level, template state. Use before view-dependent tools (tags, dimensions, colouring). [Registry tool v1, View, transaction=none. Registry tools run stored, reviewed C# inside Revit — prefer them over execute_revit_code for the same task.]

name: get_material_quantities
title: Get material quantities
description: Material take-off: per material name/class, total area (m²), volume (m³), element count and element ids. Optionally restricted to categories (BuiltInCategory names) or to the current selection. [Registry tool v1, Data, transaction=none. Registry tools run stored, reviewed C# inside Revit — prefer them over execute_revit_code for the same task.]

maxElementIdsPerMaterial.description: Cap on element ids listed per material

name: get_revit_context
title: Get Revit context
description: Returns the current Revit session: version, active document title/path, whether it is a family or read-only, display length unit, active view, open documents, whether code execution is enabled, and optionally the current selection as {id, category, name}. Call this before execute_revit_code so the script matches the real document.

includeSelection.description: Include the elements currently selected in Revit (id, category, name).

name: get_run
title: Get a past run
description: Details of one run from the history (runId comes back from the execute tool, run_tool and test_tool): outcome, args, the code when it was a successful ad-hoc script, and — when the host application is reachable — an analysis listing hard-coded literals (line, value, variable) and the args keys already read. Use it before propose_tool to decide which literals become parameters.

analyze.description: Analyse the code (guard, compile, literals) through the host application

name: get_selected_elements
title: Get selected elements
description: Elements currently selected in Revit (id, uniqueId, name, category, type, family, level). Empty list when nothing is selected. [Registry tool v1, Generic, transaction=none. Registry tools run stored, reviewed C# inside Revit — prefer them over execute_revit_code for the same task.]

limit.description: Maximum elements to return (0 = no limit)

name: get_tool
title: Get a registry tool
description: Full record of one stored tool: metadata, input schema, examples, C# code (optional), run statistics and recent runs.

recentRuns.description: How many recent runs to include (0–50)

name: inspect_type
title: Inspect a host API type
description: Reflects over an API type loaded in the running host application (Revit or AutoCAD) and returns its public members as C#-like signatures (kind: property | method | field | event). Use it to confirm exact method names and parameters before writing a script.

typeName.description: Type name, e.g. 'Wall' or 'FilteredElementCollector' in Revit, 'Polyline' or 'LayerTableRecord' in AutoCAD, or a fully qualified name such as 'Autodesk.Revit.DB.Structure.Rebar'.

memberFilter.description: Optional case-insensitive substring to keep only matching member names, e.g. 'Create'.

maxMembers.description: Maximum number of members to return (default 100, max 500).

name: manage_tool
title: Deprecate, quarantine or restore a tool
description: deprecate: retire a tool (never runs again until restored). quarantine: pull it from tools/list. restore: back to draft so it can be tested and published again.

annotations.title: Deprecate, quarantine or restore a tool

name: operate_element
title: Operate on elements
description: Act on elements by id: Select, SetColor (RGB, view override with solid fill), SetTransparency (0–100), Highlight (red), Hide, TempHide, Isolate, Unhide, ResetIsolate (clears temporary hide/isolate), Delete. View operations target the active view. SelectionBox is interactive and not available through MCP. Use dryRun for Delete. [Registry tool v1, View, transaction=auto. Registry tools run stored, reviewed C# inside Revit — prefer them over execute_revit_code for the same task.]

elementIds.description: Element ids (may be empty for ResetIsolate)

dryRun.description: Run the tool, then roll everything back. Use first on a model you care about.

name: propose_tool
title: Propose a new registry tool
description: Package a working C# script as a reusable tool (status draft). Replace every literal that may change between calls with args.<Kind>("key") and declare each key in inputSchema (JSON Schema object: string/number/integer/boolean/array/object, required, default, description). The code is guard-checked and compiled inside the host application but not run. Give ≥ 2 examples with different args; test_tool runs them. Returns a validation report; fix errors and call again. Use newVersion=true to replace the code of an existing tool.

description.description: What the tool does, for search and for the reviewer (≥ 20 chars)

category.description: One of the host's categories (search_tools lists them): Architecture | Structure | MEP | Annotation | View | Data | Generic for Revit, Drawing | Layer | Block | Annotation | Layout | Data | Generic for AutoCAD

inputSchema.description: JSON Schema of the args object

code.description: Script body: same globals as the execute tool plus args; must end with return

title.description: Human title, e.g. 'Colour beams by type'

transaction.description: auto (the bridge wraps the run in a transaction) | manual (Revit: the code opens its own Transaction; AutoCAD: same as auto) | none (read-only)

sourceRunId.description: runId of the execute run this comes from (see get_run)

newVersion.description: Propose a new version of an existing tool name

name: publish_tool
title: Publish a registry tool
description: Request publication of a tested tool. Policy manual (default): the tool becomes pending_approval, a review file is written and a human must run the server's `registry approve <name>` command (`<server>.exe registry --help`; or set status=published in tool.json). Policy auto: tested tools publish immediately. Published tools appear in tools/list of every running server.

name: run_tool
title: Run a registry tool
description: Run a stored tool from the registry with the given args (must match its inputSchema from search_tools / get_tool). Same result shape as the execute tool. Draft / tested / pending tools need allowUnpublished=true. Use dryRun=true first for tools that modify the document.

allowUnpublished.description: Allow running a tool that is not published yet

name: search_tools
title: Search the tool registry
description: Search the registry of stored tools for this host (Revit or AutoCAD) BEFORE writing code with the execute tool (execute_revit_code / execute_autocad_code). Full-text over name, description, tags and examples, ranked by relevance × stability × status. Returns each tool's inputSchema so it can be called directly by name (published tools are real MCP tools) or through run_tool. Empty query lists tools (optionally by category).

query.description: What you want to do, in any language, e.g. 'tạo lưới trục', 'color beams by type', 'room schedule'

category.description: One of the host's categories (search_tools lists them): Architecture | Structure | MEP | Annotation | View | Data | Generic for Revit, Drawing | Layer | Block | Annotation | Layout | Data | Generic for AutoCAD

includeUnpublished.description: Also return draft / tested / pending tools (they need allowUnpublished=true in run_tool)

name: tag_all_rooms

Rooms already tagged in the view are skipped. tagTypeId picks a RoomTagType; otherwise the first loaded room tag type is used. [Registry tool v1, Annotation, transaction=auto. Registry tools run stored, reviewed C# inside Revit — prefer them over execute_revit_code for the same task.]

dryRun.description: Run the tool, then roll everything back. Use first on a model you care about.

annotations.title: Tag rooms in the current view

name: tag_all_walls

Walls already tagged in the view are skipped. tagTypeId picks a wall tag family type (OST_WallTags); otherwise the first loaded one is used. [Registry tool v1, Annotation, transaction=auto. Registry tools run stored, reviewed C# inside Revit — prefer them over execute_revit_code for the same task.]

dryRun.description: Run the tool, then roll everything back. Use first on a model you care about.

annotations.title: Tag walls in the current view

name: test_tool
title: Test a registry tool
description: Run a tool's examples (or the given cases) inside the host application with dryRun — every change is rolled back — and record the outcomes. All cases passing moves a draft to tested. realRun=true commits the changes (only on a scratch model).

cases.description: Optional cases [{"title": "...", "args": {...}}]; default = the tool's examples
